about: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? shows a contestant on the quiz show set with eyes bulging and mouth slightly open behind a thick mustache, staring down at the glowing blue question bar and four answer slots marked A, B, C and D. His panicked face suggests he has no idea which option is right, or knows the answer and hates it. Captions turn the screen into a multiple choice quiz about everyday life, usually with four answers that are all bad, or three silly options and one painfully honest one.
origin: The layout copies the question-and-answer graphics of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, the quiz show that started on British TV in 1998 and spread to dozens of countries. It has been a fill-in template for years.
usage:
There are five boxes. The first goes in the long bar at the top and holds the question. The next four go in A, B, C and D in reading order.

The funniest versions make the question sound easy and the answers reveal a joke: all four options are the same, every option is a disaster, or D is the brutally honest one. Keep each answer to one to three words so they fit the slots. Debugging, homework, budgets, relationship texts and gaming strategy all work.
